findings.title: Incomplete Prototype Pollution Protection via Section Name
findings.recommendation: Strictly block 'constructor' and 'prototype' in addition to '__proto__', or validate section names against an allowlist and ensure objects are initialized with Object.create(null) or guarded against prototype traversal.

evaluations.reasoning: The diff only special-cases section === '__proto__'. Every other section name still goes through `p = out[section] = out[section] || {}`, which reads inherited properties. For `[constructor]`, `out['constructor']` is the inherited `Object` function and is truthy, so `p` becomes `Object`. Any `key=value` line that follows is then written onto the global `Object` constructor function, which is a global mutation driven by untrusted input. Inherited names such as `[toString]` and `[hasOwnProperty]` have the same problem, because `p` becomes an inherited function and gets written to. The lines 13-16 locator covers the new guard and the following assignment, so it is accurate. The finding is weaker than stated in two ways. First, 'prototype' is not exploitable as a section name: `out['prototype']` is undefined on a plain object, so it just creates an own property. Second, writing to `Object` itself does not pollute `Object.prototype` and does not reach instances. Reaching `Object.prototype` would take a second traversal step (`constructor.prototype`), and the diff shows no dotted-path handling or key-level nesting. The key-assignment code outside the diff context was not visible, so I could not confirm that. The CWE-1321 classification is reasonable (improperly controlled modification of object prototype attributes), though the impact is narrower than 'prototype pollution' implies. 'High' looks overstated, and 'medium' fits better.
